newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market up to 12.7 vs 10.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market up to 12.7 vs 10.4 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose to 12.7 percent on Thursday from 10.4 the previous day amid strained liquidity, dealers said.
Daily settlements totalled 31.8 million kuna against a 57 million demand.
Fresh trade was put at 27.8 million kuna and comprised mostly call money loans granted at an unchanged 10.5 percent.
Term loans were granted at higher rates between 11 percent for four-day funds and 18 percent for 90-day borrowings.
One-month interbank funds were rolled over at 15 percent, up from 11 percent on Wednesday.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Friday firmer at 6.0418 against the dollar and 3.5725 against the German mark. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
